display_title: kriegmate: Adversarial Monte Carlo COA Analysis
one_liner: A terrain-aware stochastic combat simulation, company team to brigade, wrapped in a full simulation-analysis toolkit: paired COA comparison with common random numbers, Kim-Nelson selection, Gaussian-process and Sobol sensitivity, and history-matching calibration.
problem: Comparing courses of action with a stochastic combat model is only useful if the comparison is statistically honest (paired, interval-bounded, selection-bias-aware), the discretization is checked, and the parameters have a defined path from notional to calibrated.
approach: I built an entity engine that runs on OpenStreetMap, DEM or synthetic ground: detection hazard, multinomial-logit target choice, circular-normal hit probability, suppression, and Beta breakpoints, with named random substreams so two courses of action share random numbers. Around it I built the analysis toolkit: Wilson, delta and sup-t intervals, Kaplan-Meier and Aalen-Johansen for censored outcomes, Kim-Nelson ranking and selection, a Latin hypercube design with a stochastic-kriging Gaussian process and Saltelli-Jansen Sobol indices, and history matching with implausibility waves and a held-out terrain coverage check. An aggregate brigade engine is derived as a mean-field limit of the entity kill chain and bias-corrected against it.
decision_relevance: Supports course-of-action analysis, which scheme of maneuver is better and with what confidence, and demonstrates the verification, validation and calibration process that Army analytic organizations apply to combat models.

headline_results.claim: Paired course-of-action comparison with common random numbers: support-by-fire wins 0.678 [0.658, 0.699] against maneuver at 0.649 [0.628, 0.670], 2,000 replications each, paired difference +0.029 [+0.009, +0.050]. Sharing random numbers halved the variance of the comparison
Sobol sensitivity analysis: probability of kill at tank range dominates the outcome (total-order index 0.61-0.79), with a Gaussian-process metamodel at leave-one-out R2 0.75-0.86
Kim-Nelson ranking and selection, history-matching calibration, and a 47-suite test harness that runs the engine, the estimators and the calibration in under 11 minutes
Convergence testing showed the 25 m grid is not converged against 12.5 m, so the model is used to compare plans rather than to predict absolute probabilities

limitations: Parameters are notional; nothing is fitted to or checked against real data
Absolute win probabilities are partly a grid artifact; only fixed-cell paired comparisons are defensible
Brigade table runs at n=20 replications; raising it costs about an hour of CPU
blockers_before_featuring: OWNER DECISION: notional force-quality and C2 scores for Russia, China and Iran (sim/nations.py, sim/c2.py) — confirm no prepublication/PAO review is required (DoDI 5230.29)
Cell size is not converged; no absolute probability from this model should appear as a result until the sweep extends to 6.25 m
Nothing is validated against real data; the site must label this a methods demonstration in progress
GitHub repo description still reads 'Mathematically rigorous combat simulation' (remote metadata, must be changed by the owner)
caveat: Parameters are notional. The model is verified against its specification, not validated against real engagements.
